incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-32178 — LB healthcheck failures in us-west-2. Escalation policy: network-oncall -> sre-oncall.

pagerduty-bot: Incident created: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/PD-32178 (priority: P1)

alex (oncall): ack'd. I'm on it, standing up in #incidents. quick check — any customer reports?

dina (support): got 3 tickets from EU customers reporting 502s since ~22:05 UTC. forwarding one: "api.redwood.io 502 Bad Gateway"

maria (network-eng): seeing spikes in TLS handshake failures on ALB target group via CloudWatch: target response codes 502/504 and unhealthy host count rising.

sam (sre): same — app logs show rapid upstream connection resets to inference workers. might be backend saturation or connection limits.

alex (oncall): status page?

lee (eng-platform): posting status: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/PD-32178 — initial impact: some traffic to inference-hosts in us-west-2 failing healthchecks, automatic failover to other regions observed.

maria (network-eng): digging into ALB logs. early grep: TLS alert "handshake_failure" and "bad_certificate" in small subset. but majority are target timeouts. suspecting a mix: partial TLS handshake errors + backend overload.

sam (sre): could be NAT gateway ephemeral port exhaustion — lots of outbound connections from workers to a 3rd-party keyserver? checking metrics.

alex (oncall): runbook step 1: confirm scope. alex -> maria to confirm LB group health and certificate status. sam -> check host CPU, socket counts, and NAT metrics.

maria (network-eng): ALB target-group tg-infer-usw2: healthy=3 unhealthy=7 (total 10). TLS cert for edge look OK (rotated 17 days ago). No cert mismatch for SNI. ALB logs show client TLS failures from clients spanning multiple ASNs.

sam (sre): host metrics: a few inference hosts show fd counts near 64k, lots of CLOSE_WAIT. connection reset rate high. nat-gw ephemeral ports in use: 61k/64k on the public NAT. that explains timeouts.

alex (oncall): okay that lines up — ephemeral exhaustion causing upstream connection failures -> targets flapping unhealthy. mitigation options: 1) increase NAT capacity / add another NAT gateway 2) scale inference hosts down to reduce outbound fanout? 3) use TCP proxying to reduce ephemeral usage.

lee (eng-platform): quick patch: we've got a spare NAT in same AZ. I can add it to the route table. pushing the change now (will take ~30s to propagate).

incident-bot: Change scheduled: add-nat-gw-usw2 (initiated by lee).

lee (eng-platform): added nat-gw-02 to subnet route table. verifying.

maria (network-eng): re-checking target group health: healthy->6, unhealthy->4. TLS handshake errors dropping.

sam (sre): ephemeral ports now 18k/64k on the main NAT nodes. FD counts decreasing, CLOSE_WAIT clearing. backend rps stable.

dina (support): updated affected tickets: telling customers we're investigating networking/NAT capacity; next update in 15m.

alex (oncall): hold for 10m, watch for recurring failures. if more flaps, plan B: temporary traffic shift away from us-west-2 (route weight shift) and open PD P2 followup.

maria (network-eng): quick follow-ups: origin keepalive settings are low (5s) causing high outbound connection churn for short-lived upstream calls. recommend increasing keepalive and enabling connection pooling in the inference service. filing a config PR: https://git.internal/redwood/inference/pulls/4521

sam (sre): adding temporary socket tuning on hosts: sysctl net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range expanded and tcp_fin_timeout lowered. applying via runbook script:```
# runbook
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range="1024 65535"
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout=30
```

lee (eng-platform): applied tuning to rolling group of 5 hosts, will continue rolling.

alex (oncall): impact assessment: customers in EU and US-west saw elevated 502/504s for ~22:05-22:20 UTC. Root cause: NAT ephemeral port exhaustion causing backend upstream resets; exacerbated by short keepalive settings.

dina (support): drafting status update to customers: ETA for full mitigation ~1h, will follow with postmortem.

alex (oncall): moving to steady-state monitoring. will keep this thread open. handing off to maria (network) for next 2 hours for config PR + ALB health. I'll hand off oncall at 23:00 UTC to sam.

maria (network-eng): ack handoff. I'll validate PR and monitor TG health for the next 2h.

sam (sre): I'll take oncall at 23:00 UTC. prepping notes: see runbook steps + PR link.

alex (oncall): final note: P1->resolved for active customer impact (partial reduction after NAT add). PD incident will be updated to P2 for followup work. Next: postmortem to cover why autoscaling or NAT capacity alert didn't trigger sooner.

incident-bot: Incident PD-32178 status changed: acknowledged -> mitigated.

dina (support): posted update to affected customers and internal status page.

maria (network-eng): monitoring shows stable healthy=9/10 now, TLS alerts at baseline. I'll keep an eye.

sam (sre): noted. thanks all. handoff complete at 23:00 UTC.

alex (oncall): closing active pager. follow-up tasks assigned: NAT autoscale runbook, keepalive defaults change, postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident PD-32178 marked mitigated. Follow-up task channel #postmortems to create timeline.
